rules.judge: Does a trigger hook (useTaskTrigger, useRealtimeTaskTrigger or useRealtimeTaskTriggerWithStreams from @trigger.dev/react-hooks) receive as accessToken a Public Access Token created with read scopes (auth.createPublicToken), or a read-only token passed through from the backend, instead of a trigger token from auth.createTriggerPublicToken? Report only when the token's origin is visible in the code or the same component; if the origin is unknown, do not report.
rules.message: a trigger hook is given a read-scoped public access token; trigger hooks need a trigger token
rules.fix: create the token on the backend with auth.createTriggerPublicToken(taskId) and pass it as accessToken

rules.message: imports @trigger.dev/react-hooks and has no "use client" directive; in an App Router tree this file is a Server Component, where these hooks cannot run
rules.fix: add "use client"; as the first line if this file is in a Next.js App Router (RSC) tree

rules.message: useRun() polls on refreshInterval > 0; useRealtimeRun() subscribes to the run by ID instead

rules.judge: Is this a component or hook that subscribes to a run (useRealtimeRun or useRealtimeTaskTrigger) and reads only status-like fields (status, a progress or completion badge), never run.payload or run.output, while the hook options have no skipColumns? Report only when no payload or output field is read from the returned run.
rules.message: subscribes to the full run for status only; payload and output are streamed without being read
rules.fix: pass skipColumns: ["payload", "output"] in the hook options

rules.judge: Does a realtime hook (useRealtimeRun, useRealtimeTaskTrigger) receive an id that can be undefined at first render, such as handle?.id from a trigger whose handle does not exist yet, with no enabled option in its options? Report only when the id can be undefined.
rules.message: a realtime hook is given an id that is undefined until the trigger returns, and has no enabled option
rules.fix: pass enabled: !!handle in the hook options

rules.judge: Is there a for-await loop over runs.subscribeToRunsWithTag(...) or runs.subscribeToBatch(...) whose body contains no break and no return? Report only when no break or return can exit the loop.
rules.message: for-await loop over runs.subscribeToRunsWithTag / runs.subscribeToBatch has no break; the iterator never completes by itself
rules.fix: break (or return) once the completion condition is met

rules.message: client-side code calls fetch() on a wait token's token.url; that webhook URL is for server-to-server use and has no CORS headers
rules.fix: complete from the browser with the token's publicAccessToken (CORS-enabled endpoint), or use useWaitToken

rules.message: wait.createToken() is called without a timeout, so the token has none
rules.fix: pass a timeout, e.g. wait.createToken({ timeout: '10m' })

rules.message: hard-codes https://api.trigger.dev as the API base URL; self-hosted installs set TRIGGER_API_URL instead
rules.fix: read the base URL from TRIGGER_API_URL (or pass baseURL to configure) instead of a literal

rules.message: app code imports a task module as a value; only its type is needed to trigger it
rules.fix: import type { task } from the module and call tasks.trigger<typeof task>("task-id", payload)
rules.judge: Confirm the importing file is app or client code. A task file importing a sibling task by value is fine; an app route, page or client component importing task modules by value pulls task code into the app bundle.
